# `m.options.bars`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Aggregate bars (open, high, low, close, volume) of US-listed options contracts.

```python
m.options.bars(symbols, timespan, *, multiplier=1, adjusted=True)
```

| Plan | Day Aggregates (flat files) | Minute Aggregates (flat files) | Custom Bars (OHLC) (REST) | Aggregates (Per Minute) (WebSocket) | Aggregates (Per Second) (WebSocket) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Options Basic | Not included | Not included | End-of-day, 2 years | Not included | Not included |
| Options Starter | End-of-day, 2 years | End-of-day, 2 years | 15-minute delayed, 2 years | 15-minute delayed | 15-minute delayed |
| Options Developer | End-of-day, 4 years | End-of-day, 4 years | 15-minute delayed, 4 years | 15-minute delayed | 15-minute delayed |
| Options Advanced | End-of-day, All history | End-of-day, All history | Real-time, All history | Real-time | Real-time |
| Options Business | End-of-day, All history | End-of-day, All history | Real-time, All history | Real-time | Not included |
| Options Business + Expansion |  |  | Real-time, All history |  | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `optionsTicker` parameter; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given option contract." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the bar, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `TimestampStart` for an intraday or 1-day bar, and null for a bar that spans more than one date (several days, a week or longer, or an intraday bar that crosses midnight). Joining an intraday row to the same day's daily bar on `Date` attaches values not known until that day ended, and a null `Date` matches another null, so join longer bars on `TimestampEnd`. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the bar's window, as an Instant. A bar of a day or longer starts at 00:00 New York time of its window's first day (a week's Monday, a month's, quarter's, or year's first weekday), whichever source serves it. A bar of a day or longer stamped at a time or on a day Massive is not known to use keeps that stamp, has a null `Date`, and ends one period after it, with a WARNING, since which day it covers is not known. Every other stamp, as each source sends it (quoted next), is moved there. From REST `t`: "The Unix millisecond timestamp for the start of the aggregate window."; flat files `window_start`: "The Unix nanosecond timestamp for the start of the aggregate window."; WebSocket `s`: "The start timestamp of this aggregate window in Unix Milliseconds." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the bar's window, as an Instant: the first instant at which the bar is complete, so an as-of join on it, `t.aj(bars, on=["Symbol", "Timestamp>=TimestampEnd"])`, never attaches a bar that is still open. It is when the window closes, not when Massive published the bar, and Massive may correct a bar later. An intraday bar ends its length after its start; a bar of a day or longer at 00:00 New York time after its window's last day. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC option root, read from `Symbol`: the symbol without its `O:` prefix and its last 15 characters (expiry, type, and strike), such as `SPXW` for `O:SPXW251219C06000000`. It is never mapped to the underlying: an adjusted contract keeps its own root, such as `AAPL1`. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Open` | double | The open price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `High` | double | The highest price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Low` | double | The lowest price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Close` | double | The close price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Volume` | double | The trading volume of the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted like the prices when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a volume from before a split is restated in the split's terms (multiplied by its ratio). With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Vwap` | double | The volume weighted average price. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST, WebSocket |
| `Transactions` | long | The number of transactions in the aggregate window. | REST, flat files |
| `AccumulatedVolume` | long | Today's accumulated volume. | WebSocket |
| `OfficialOpen` | double | Today's official opening price. | WebSocket |
| `DayVwap` | double | Today's volume weighted average price. | WebSocket |
| `AverageTradeSize` | long | The average trade size for this aggregate window. | WebSocket |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
